topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe foundational cancer treatment modalities—surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their mechanisms, toxicities, and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit tumor-specific vulnerabilities, such as hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene targeting, kinase inhibitors, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small molecule inhibitors targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the mutational, bypass, and addiction mechanisms that lead to drug resistance.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover targeted antibody therapeutics that recognize tumor surface antigens to inhibit signaling, direct immune-mediated killing, or deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the role of host immunity in cancer and therapeutic modalities that reactivate or engineer T cells to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, progress, and future directions in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate historical progress in cancer survival alongside persistent clinical challenges, emerging treatment paradigms, and clinical trial dilemmas.
